item.text:
Continuing the audit, this turn I closed out the remaining analogous local paths and refreshed the report.

Key checks:
- **Snapshot restore on startup** (`api.go restoreSnapshot`): the snapshot *meta* is decoded by the snapshot store (decode errors are handled / the next snapshot is tried), and v0 snapshots use `decodePeers` (returns an error). So the local startup path does **not** panic on corrupt input, unlike the network handlers in F1/F3 — a useful contrast that further localizes the defect to the three RPC call sites rather than "decoding in general." `shouldSnapshot`/`takeSnapshot` correctly record the committed configuration and require `applyIndex >= committedConfigurationIndex`.
- Confirmed `ProtocolVersionMin=0`, `ProtocolVersionMax=3`, so the reachability claim (header version 2..3 passes `checkRPCHeader` on a default node) is exact.

I updated the report's coverage map (§4) with these, and adjusted the "unresolved work" (§5) since leadership-transfer edge cases now have some coverage from the transfer-churn stress.

**Where this stands.** The audit has saturated its findable surface on this pristine baseline:

- Three concrete, reproducible defects (F1/F2/F3), one localized class of RPC-reachable, unauthenticated, remote-crash defects, inherited from upstream `hashicorp/raft@v1.7.3` (tree byte-identical to the release; nothing claimed as injected).
- Everything else checked — consensus safety under partition/heal and leadership-transfer churn, crash/restart durability incl. snapshot restore, `-race`, snapshot retention, config-change semantics, and the analogous decode paths — is clean or benign.
- All evidence reproduces with `bash audit/run_all.sh`; `go vet`/`go build` clean; the intentionally-crashing end-to-end case is env-guarded.

Report: [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-09_08-06-10-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/report.md) (18 sections, 566 lines; 13 artifacts under `work/audit/`).

If further budget is allocated, the only materially new work left is external: (1) run the ~15 TCP/loopback test groups via the private-loopback `isolated_exec` to (a) confirm the F1–F3 network reachability end-to-end over real TCP and (b) clear the socket-blocked tests; and (2) byte-verify/run `fuzzy/` and `raft-compat/` once a reference or their dependencies are available. Within the current sandbox I have nothing further that changes the conclusions.
